items.title: Google DeepMind releases Gemini Robotics 2.5 vision-language-action model
items.summary_en: DeepMind's blog describes Gemini Robotics 2.5 as its most capable robotics model so far, able to learn many everyday skills. It is rolling out to robotics partners first. The post reports large gains on tabletop pick-and-place tasks over the previous model and adds reasoning guidance meant to help avoid physical hazards.
items.notes: Direct WebFetch of deepmind.google failed (host not in the session's allowed network domains). Details come from search-result snippets of the official page, not the full text, so figures are unverified. The date comes from search-tool output. A companion X post exists: https://x.com/GoogleDeepMind/status/2120169787896525104 (not opened). A secondary-source report cited a Mercedes-Benz pilot figure that I could not confirm on the primary page.

items.title: AlphaGenome 2 announced for predicting how DNA variants affect gene expression
items.summary_en: DeepMind presents AlphaGenome 2 as a follow-up to the original AlphaGenome, which predicts how DNA sequence variants affect molecular activity in cells. According to the post snippet, it identifies nearly twice as many expression-changing variants as the prior best model. It is available for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API, with a private preview for commercial research.
items.notes: Publication date is NOT confirmed. The page was not fetched (deepmind.google blocked) and the snippet shows no date. 2026-11-10 is an estimate from secondary reporting that places it in the same week as Gemini Robotics 2.5, so verify it before use. The full text was not read.

coverage_note: Direct access to deepmind.google was blocked in this session, so all items rest on search-result snippets of official pages and are marked primary-inferred. Two official posts appear to fall in the window: Gemini Robotics 2.5 and AlphaGenome 2. Other items surfaced only through secondary sources, which are excluded here. These include a Nov 8 remark attributed to Pushmeet Kohli about a 'phase transition' in scientific discovery, with releases coming within weeks, and August 2026 leadership changes (Hassabis to chair and Alphabet chief scientist, Kavukcuoglu leading Gemini) with reported departures to a startup called Discovery Loop. Secondary reports on Gemini 4 naming conflict, so treat Gemini 4 details as unconfirmed. I found no official source for any of these. Allowing deepmind.google and blog.google in the session's network settings would let a re-run verify the dates and full text.
